main_text.p: cuantur plurima euacuatione. Vtrisque cum cibum fastidiunt, piscium salitorum vsum potius incommodo fore, quàm adiumento opinor. Sed neque oliuæ conditæ hos meliores reddent. Sed si succum perdicis ijs obtulisset, offamque panis in vino odorifero madentem et similia, citius his appetentiā reduceret, cum à prædictis causis cibū fastidirent. Sed indistinctè admodum multa postmodum connumerat quæ fastidium discutiunt ad hunc modum. Ex prouocantibus appetitum sunt cap,,pares præparatæ, menta, cepa, oliuæ, piper, caryophylli, galanga, acetum, acetosa, almuri, allia, cepa, opoponacum & mel. Hæc ille, quibus in verbis multa absque vlla methodo connumerauit remedia, quibus cōueniant dispositionibus ea non adaptans. Quorum alia ex eo quia exiccant & exasperant appetentiam inducunt, vt cappares præparatæ & menta. Alia ob id quod astringendo exiccāt, vt acetum, acetosa, muria, & condita oliua. Alia quia exiccando excrementa à ventriculo excernunt, vt allium, piper. Alia quia mordendo

page.notes: Marginal marks at left (quotation-style signs beside the lines "pares" to "ri, allia") and a small dot beside "merat" are printed marks; the signs are transcribed only as a note. Some words are doubtful in the scan, notably "dispositionibus" and "appetentiā"; the "cōueniant" abbreviation is retained as printed. Last line of the column ends with "mordendo" set right-aligned.
